title: A1-07 · Nationality and adjective of relation (nisba)

blocks.text: A1-07 · Nationality and adjective of relation (nisba)
Lesson overview

From ⁧مِصْر⁩ Egypt is formed ⁧مِصْرِيّ⁩ • Egyptian • Egyptian from ⁧عَرَب⁩ Arabic ⁧عَرَبِيّ⁩ (a) Arabic; from ⁧شُرْطَة⁩ Police ⁧شُرْطِيّ⁩ "Cop" is a cop. The suffix -iyy , called nisba () (the report) transforms a name into an adjective that indicates belonging. It is one of the most productive tools in Arabic: you will use it for nationality and languages, and then you will recognize it in hundreds of political, institutional and technical adjectives.

rows: 6–7 hours · one week (week 22 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-07), voice synthesis script, a map of the Arab world
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. to form the male and female nyba from the names of the main countries;
2. say and ask for nationality, provenance and residence;
3. Grant the nysba as an adjective ( ⁧رَجُلٌ مِصْرِيٌّ، الطَّالِبَةُ المِصْرِيَّةُ⁩ );
4. appointing languages ( ⁧العَرَبِيَّةُ، الإِيطَالِيَّةُ⁩ …);
5. distinguish citizenship, ethnicity and language in presentations;
6. read educational charts and present people from different countries.

2. How the Nisba Forms
The basic rule has three steps: remove the article, remove the termination -a / -ā / -iyā name, add ⁧ـِيّ⁩ (male) or ⁧ـِيَّة⁩ (female).

Because the termination falls. The nisba attaches itself to the root of the name: in ⁧سُورِيَا⁩ , ⁧إِيطَالِيَا⁩ , ⁧فَرَنْسَا⁩ the -iyā / -ā final is perceived as nonessential part and falls. In ⁧السُّعُودِيَّة⁩ the name of the country is already a female nyba (-[the kingdom] Saudi Arabia): removing the ⁧ة⁩ stays ⁧سُعُودِيّ⁩ . Not just countries. The same adjective form rule from any name: ⁧عَرَب⁩ → ⁧عَرَبِيّ⁩ "Arabic" is the word "Arabic"; ⁧دَوْلَة⁩ → ⁧دَوْلِيّ⁩ International (L0), ⁧سِيَاسَة⁩ → ⁧سِيَاسِيّ⁩ Politically speaking, this is the case (L0), ⁧شُرْطَة⁩ → ⁧شُرْطِيّ⁩ , ⁧أَمْن⁩ → ⁧أَمْنِيّ⁩ Safety-belted, ⁧رَسْم⁩ → ⁧رَسْمِيّ⁩ Official: Many adjectives of the print that you will read from B1 I'm Nisba. Cases to memorize. ⁧أَفْغَانِسْتَان⁩ → ⁧أَفْغَانِيّ⁩ (fall -istān), but ⁧بَاكِسْتَان⁩ → ⁧بَاكِسْتَانِيّ⁩ . The cities: ⁧بَغْدَاد⁩ → ⁧بَغْدَادِيّ⁩ , ⁧دِمَشْق⁩ → ⁧دِمَشْقِيّ⁩ , ⁧بَيْرُوت⁩ → ⁧بَيْرُوتِيّ⁩ . With plurals and other foreign names there are other exceptions: you will see them when they are needed. The pronunciation of -iyy. Inside the sentence the šadda You hear: miṣriyyun ; pause becomes ī long: miṣrī . To the female, the double always remains: miṣriyya .
3. The nyba as an adjective
The nyba is an adjective like the others (A1-03, A1-04): follows the name and generally agrees and determination.

Nationality as predicate: without article. "I am Egyptian" = ⁧أَنَا مِصْرِيٌّ⁩ . ⁧أَنَا المِصْرِيُّ⁩ I am the Egyptian (of which we speak) A1-02. With the institutions. The government, the ministry, the army of a country are indicated with the nysba: ⁧الجَيْشُ اللُّبْنَانِيُّ⁩ The Lebanese army shall be: ⁧وِزَارَةُ الدَّاخِلِيَّةِ المِصْرِيَّةُ⁩ The Ministry of the Interior of Egypt. It's the structure of news headlines.

5. Citizenship, ethnicity, language
In documents, citizenship is ⁧الجِنْسِيَّة⁩ al-ǧinsiyya : ⁧الجِنْسِيَّةُ⁩ : . ⁧مِصْرِيَّةٌ⁩ It does not always coincide with the belonging of a person or his language:
• an Iraqi or Syrian citizen may be Arabic ( ⁧عَرَبِيّ⁩ ) or Kurdish ( ⁧كُرْدِيّ⁩ ), and have as first language Arabic or Kurdish;
• a Moroccan or Algerian citizen may be Arabic or Amazigh ( ⁧أَمَازِيغِيّ⁩ ), and speak Arabic, a language amazigh or both;
• ⁧عَرَبِيّ⁩ indicates membership of Arabic language and culture, not citizenship.

In professional communication, you use the term that the person uses for himself and, in documents, always distinguish the three data. Confounding them is one of the most common mistakes in journalistic descriptions.
6. Pronunciation

The doubles of the nyba. Inside the sentence: ʿirāqiyyun min Baġdād , šurṭiyyun īṭāliyy(one) . Pause: ʿirāqī , īṭālī . To the female always -iyya . ⁧ع⁩ and ⁧ق⁩ in ⁧عِرَاقِيّ⁩ . One ʿayn at the beginning and one qāf in the center: two sounds absent in English in the same word. Irāki with k is the Italian pronunciation to be avoided. ⁧ص⁩ in ⁧البَصْرَة⁩ , ⁧ح⁩ in ⁧حَلَب⁩ . Basra begins with the article and a ṣād Emphasis: al-Baṣra . Aleppo is ⁧حَلَب⁩ Ḥalab , ḥāʾ. Names of foreign countries. ⁧إِيطَالِيَا⁩ , ⁧أَلْمَانِيَا⁩ , ⁧فَرَنْسَا⁩ long vowels are written (ī, ā) and must be kept.
7. New lexicon
⁧أُرْدُنِيّ⁩ urdunī Jordanian - adjective f. ⁧أُرْدُنِيَّة⁩

Notes of use. The plural of the nysba in person is often regular (-iyyūn), but some have their own pluralities: ⁧مَغَارِبَة⁩ Moroccans (including Moroccans) ⁧عَرَب⁩ "Arabic" is equal to or greater than "Arabic"; ⁧أَكْرَاد⁩ "Kurdish." ⁧بَلَد⁩ means country, country, country, in Egypt and the Levant ⁧بَلَد⁩ It is also used for Christmas cities. ⁧مُقِيم⁩ is the word of documents: ⁧الإِقَامَة⁩ al-iqāma is the residence permit (s) or residence (s).
